### 3.2 Proposal

Two new modules. They group the code by layer: hosts and machine adapters go in `Build`, and
polynomial-time corollaries in `ClassNP`. Their imports are modules `SAT` already reaches today
(the definers of `stateWord`, `Cfg.ofWords`, `emitAction`/`emitCfg`/`emit_run`,
`FinTM.controlAction`, `Turing.Segment`, `FinTM.exists_installCallTM`/`exists_emitCallTM`,
`PolyTimeComputable`, `FinTM.inputSymbol_at`). Their exact module names must be read off the tree;
they are not in the bundle. Neither new module may import `SAT`. **`SAT` gains one or two
imports. That is a new import into a frozen file, flagged for Seyoon.** `Hardness` reaches the new
modules through `SAT` and needs no new import.

- **M-T** `TCSlib/Complexity/ClassNP/OneWayTransducer.lean` (SG1-A). It could instead go into the
  colleague-owned `ClassNP/Transducer.lean` if that file's transducer gained a final emission.
  That would be a colleague interface change, so the new module is the default.
- **M-C** `TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/CleanCall.lean` (SG1-B, and SG1-C if run), with
  its polynomial-time corollaries in `ClassNP/CleanCallPoly.lean`. Alternatively, put the two
  corollaries beside `FinTM.exists_installCallTM`/`exists_emitCallTM`, of which they are direct
  consequences; that saves one module header (about 25–35 lines).

The proposed statements below are uncompiled. Names are proposals for Seyoon. Docstrings follow
`policy.md` §2–3: these are construction glue with no textbook counterpart, so they carry no
declaration-level tag. Each module's `## References` cites [AB09, §1.2] for the multitape model.

**SG1-A (M-T, namespace `Complexity`).**

```lean
/-- The word computed by a finite one-way transducer with state set `S`: on input bit `b` in
state `q` it emits `emit q b` (at most one bit) and moves to `next q b`; at the right end it
emits `finish q`. -/
def oneWayWord {S : Type} (next : S → Bool → S) (emit : S → Bool → Option Bool)
    (finish : S → Option Bool) : S → List Bool → List Bool
  | q, [] => (finish q).toList
  | q, b :: r => (emit q b).toList ++ oneWayWord next emit finish (next q b) r

/-- `oneWayWord` on the empty word is the final emission. -/
theorem oneWayWord_nil … : oneWayWord next emit finish q [] = (finish q).toList
/-- `oneWayWord` on `b :: r` emits `emit q b` and continues from `next q b`. -/
theorem oneWayWord_cons … : oneWayWord next emit finish q (b :: r) =
    (emit q b).toList ++ oneWayWord next emit finish (next q b) r

/-- The zero-work-tape machine realizing `oneWayWord … start`: one right move per input bit,
then one halting transition at the right blank. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false })]
def oneWayTM {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S] (next : S → Bool → S)
    (emit : S → Bool → Option Bool) (finish : S → Option Bool) (start : S) : FinTM Bool

/-- `oneWayTM` computes `oneWayWord … start` in time `n + 1`.
**Proof sketch.** Induct on the unread suffix. Each input bit is one transition that appends
its optional emission, and the right blank is the final halting transition. -/
theorem oneWayTM_computesFunInTime … :
    (oneWayTM next emit finish start).ComputesFunInTime
      (oneWayWord next emit finish start) (fun n => n + 1)

/-- Every finite one-way transduction is polynomial-time computable. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_oneWayWord … : PolyTimeComputable (oneWayWord next emit finish start)
```

`…MapCfg` and the run induction become `private` inside M-T. All ten twins are deleted. The
riders become citations and keep their names, so their use sites stay byte-identical:
- `satScanTM` becomes a private abbreviation of `oneWayTM step (fun _ _ => none) (some ∘ accept)`.
  `satScan_computes` follows from `oneWayTM_computesFunInTime` and the identity
  `oneWayWord step (fun _ _ => none) (some ∘ accept) q x = [accept (x.foldl step q)]` (est. 6–10
  lines). `satScanCfg`, `satScan_step` and `satScan_run` are deleted.
- `clNative_fill` is re-proved through `polyTimeComputable_oneWayWord` at constant emission;
  `clFillTM` and `clFill_run` are deleted.
- `sat_pt_tail`/`_head` cite `polyTimeComputable_tail`/`_take1`, as Hardness already does. This
  needs `SAT` to import `ClassNP/PolyTimeBlockLoop`, a decision the backlog lists as pending.
  Without that import they stay, retargeted to `oneWayWord_*`.

**SG1-B (M-C, namespace `Turing.FinTM`; corollaries in `Complexity`).**

```lean
/-- `M` is a clean module for `result`, `emit` and budget `B`: it has a work tape, and from
every untouched native input `x` and argument `arg` stored as the canonical state word, it
first halts at a positive time `t ≤ B |arg|`. It leaves the state word `result arg` with every
head at the origin and has emitted exactly `emit arg`. -/
structure CleanModule (M : FinTM Bool) (result emit : List Bool → List Bool) (B : ℕ → ℕ) :
    Prop where
  pos : 0 < M.k
  run : ∀ x arg : List Bool, ∃ t, 0 < t ∧ t ≤ B arg.length ∧
    (∀ v < t, ¬(M.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) M.tm.q₀ (stateWord M.k arg)) v).Halted) ∧
    M.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) M.tm.q₀ (stateWord M.k arg)) t =
      {Cfg.ofWords M.tm.q₀ (stateWord M.k (result arg)) with state := none, output := emit arg}

/-- Release-flag stop adapter: runs `C` from `entry`, and halts silently on the first visit to
`exit` made after at least one step (so `entry = exit` is allowed). -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false })]
def stopTM (C : FinTM Bool) (entry exit : C.State) : FinTM Bool
/-- The adapter's configuration: `c` with release flag `b` paired onto its state. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false })]
def stopCfg {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool} (b : Bool) (c : Cfg k Bool S x) :
    Cfg k Bool (Bool × S) x
/-- Before the designated exit, the adapter takes the module's physical step and raises the
release flag. -/
theorem stopTM_step … : (stopTM C entry exit).tm.step (stopCfg b c) = stopCfg true (C.tm.step c)
/-- A positive return to `exit` with the guard becomes a silent halt one step later, keeping
every seam field and the emitted output.
**Proof sketch.** Induct on prefixes. The flag is false only at time zero, the guard prevents an
early stop, and the final transition is silent. -/
theorem stopTM_runFrom_clean … : (stopTM C entry exit).tm.runFrom
    (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (false, entry) (stateWord C.k arg)) (t + 1) =
    {Cfg.ofWords (true, exit) (stateWord C.k result) with state := none, output := out}
/-- A guarded positive-return bridge contract makes `stopTM` a clean module with budget
`B + 1`. -/
theorem CleanModule.of_stop … : CleanModule (stopTM C entry exit) result emit (fun n => B n + 1)

/-- A run that starts live and halts by time `t` has a positive first halt `u ≤ t` with the same
endpoint. -/
theorem _root_.Turing.MultiTapeTM.exists_first_halt_pos … : ∃ u, 0 < u ∧ u ≤ t ∧
    (∀ v < u, ¬(tm.runFrom cfg v).Halted) ∧ tm.runFrom cfg u = tm.runFrom cfg t
/-- Two consecutive segments that both avoid `anchor`, with the seam also off it, avoid `anchor`
throughout (a corollary of `Turing.Segment.trans`). -/
theorem _root_.Turing.MultiTapeTM.avoid_add … : ∀ v < a + b, (tm.runFrom c v).state ≠ some anchor

-- ClassNP/CleanCallPoly.lean, namespace Complexity
/-- Every polynomial-time `f` has a clean install module (result `f`, no output) with a
polynomial budget in the argument length. -/
theorem exists_cleanInstall {f} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f) :
    ∃ M A d, FinTM.CleanModule M f (fun _ => []) (fun n => A * (n + 1) ^ d)
/-- Every polynomial-time `f` has a clean emit module (argument kept, output `f`) with a
polynomial budget. -/
theorem exists_cleanEmit {f} (hf : PolyTimeComputable f) :
    ∃ M A d, FinTM.CleanModule M id f (fun n => A * (n + 1) ^ d)
```

K5's `bridge_bound` becomes `private` in `CleanCallPoly`, its only consumer, so it adds no new
public API. The SG1 ledger's own kind-5 proposal (a public arithmetic lemma) is not needed.
`sat_live_prefix`/`clA5_live_prefix` are deleted, and `stopTM_runFrom_clean` cites
`runFrom_state_ne_none_of_le` directly. `exists_first_halt_pos`'s natural home is beside
`exists_first_halt` in `Finite`, but that file sits low in the import graph and adding to it
replays most of the library. So M-C is proposed, with `Finite` as Seyoon's alternative.

In the files, `SatClean`/`CLA5Clean` stay as one-line private `abbrev`s of `FinTM.CleanModule`, so
private headers stay byte-identical. Reading an abbreviation is allowed, and consumers use only
`h.1`/`h.2`, which are now structure projections. `satClean_install/_emit` and
`clA5Clean_install/_emit` stay as private citations of `exists_cleanInstall/_cleanEmit`, header
kept (R1a precedent), and so do `sat_guard_add`/`clA5_guard_add`. The large consumers
`satReduction_poly`, `clA5Round` and `clA5Output_of_nativeChunk` are then **not touched** by SG1-B.
`clA5StopTM` cannot be aliased (finding 2): its four readers are repaired through `stopTM_k`,
`stopTM_tm_q₀` and `stopTM_State`.

**SG1-C (M-C, only if run).** These are the same SAT declarations, generalized:

```lean
/-- State of the shared-bank dispatcher over a finite family of modules: the anchor, or a
module index with that module's state. -/
abbrev BankState {n : ℕ} (M : Fin n → FinTM Bool) := Unit ⊕ (Σ i, (M i).State)
theorem bankState_eq … -- abbrev lemma (TEMPLATE: new public abbrev lands with its lemma)
/-- Entry state of module `i`. -/
def bankEntry (M : Fin n → FinTM Bool) (i : Fin n) : BankState M
/-- Where module `i` returns: the entry of `next i`, or the anchor when `next i = none`. -/
def bankRet (next : Fin n → Option (Fin n)) (M) (i) : BankState M
theorem bankRet_of_some … ; theorem bankRet_of_none …
/-- Bank padding: a `k`-tape action or configuration on `K ≥ k` tapes, extra tapes blank and
stationary. -/
@[simps …] def bankPadAction … ; @[simps …] def bankPadTM … ; @[simps …] def bankPadCfg …
theorem bankPadAction_apply … ; theorem bankPadTM_runFrom … ; theorem bankPadCfg_ofWords …
/-- The finite-family dispatcher: padded modules share one `K`-tape bank; module `i` returns to
`bankRet next M i`, and the anchor dispatches to `bankEntry M loop`. -/
@[simps (config := { isSimp := false })]
def bankHostTM (M : Fin n → FinTM Bool) (next : Fin n → Option (Fin n)) (start loop : Fin n)
    (K : ℕ) (hk : ∀ i, (M i).k ≤ K) : FinTM Bool
theorem bankHostTM_initCfg … : (bankHostTM M next start loop K hk).tm.initCfg x =
    Cfg.ofWords (bankEntry M start) (stateWord K [])            -- replaces two `hi` blocks
theorem bankHostTM_step_anchor … : (bankHostTM …).tm.step
    {Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (.inl ()) (stateWord K w) with output := out} =
    {Cfg.ofWords (bankEntry M loop) (stateWord K w) with output := out}  -- replaces two `dispatch`
theorem bankHost_seam … ; theorem bankHost_call … ; theorem bankHost_clean …
```

**Policy gate.** `bankHostTM` is a dispatcher, so it is a *host* under policy §1 ("Hosts come
first"). Its public contract must carry time *and* space (head-envelope) clauses and be registered
in `machine-library-design.md` §14. `CleanModule` has no space clause, and neither do
`exists_installCallTM`/`exists_emitCallTM` as consumed here. So an envelope clause means
extending the contract and every module's proof: est. +100 to +300 lines. The consumers are
polynomial-time reductions and need no space bound. A time-only contract, with the envelope
deferred and recorded, is Seyoon's call.

**Other K3 candidates, not drop-ins.**
- `Turing.embedEmitTM` at `Fin.castLEEmb` (the inventory's suggestion). R1's transition selects
  slots through a `List.finRange … find?` lookup: `clPlacedAction_eq` (`Hardness:1915`) unfolds it
  by `change`, and item 13's `clPlacement_lookup` exists to close it. Padding through R1 would need
  a published lookup equation at `castLEEmb` or item 13's selector layer.
- `Build/EmitIterEmbed`'s public `padAction`/`embedCfg`/`embed_run` layer (ledger L311). Its
  statements are not bundled. Compare it before choosing K3's home. The `bankPad*` names above
  avoid colliding with it.

## 4. SG1-UH: the unary-clock host

**Members (measured, `Hardness`, all private; 4 definitions and 10 lemmas):**
- `clRepeatTM` 5656 (16+2), `clRepeatCfg` 5675 (7+2), `clRepeat_frame` 5684 (13+1)
- `clRepeat_call` 5704 (45+6), `clRepeat_round` 5753 (27+3), `clRepeat_complete` 5787 (31+6)
- `clRepeatWords` 5821 (2+2), `clRepeat_initial` 5825 (8+1), `clRepeatOutputTM` 5835 (3+1)
- `clRepeatOutput_compute` 5845 (41+6), `clRepeat_budget` 5961 (33+3)
- `clRepeatArgument_native` 5997 (16+2), `clA5Iter_native` 6747 (32+6),
  `clA5Iter_shrinking` 6782 (19+2)

That is 293+43 = 336 lines, with no SAT twin. **This is not copy debt.** It is a private host,
retained by Seyoon's 2026-11-07 ruling.

**Use sites:**
- **Outside the family:** `clVisitRows_native` 6040 (36), `clA5Field_native` 6841 (13),
  `clA5Decode_native` 7421 (26).
- **Inside:** the host is built on item 13: `clRepeatTM`, `clRepeat_frame`, `clRepeat_call` and
  `clRepeatOutput_compute` use `clKeepLastPlacement`, `clPlacedAction/Cfg`, `clPlaced_apply/_run`.
  It also builds on Hardness's private native loader and replay (`clPreparedTM`, `clPrepared_run`,
  `clPrepared_idle`, `clOutputTM`, `clOutputAt_compute`, `clFields`, `clNative_image`).

**Proposal if run.** Move the core host (`clRepeatTM`, `clRepeatCfg`, `_frame`, `_call`, `_round`,
`_complete`, `clRepeatWords`, `_initial`; 172 lines) into `Build` as a public unary-clock host. It
would be restated over R1 (`embedEmitTM` at `Fin.castAddEmb 1`) or over a published item-13
layout, with B1040's contract:

```lean
/-- Unary-clock repetition host: from a clean-call contract of `C` (positive first return from
`entry` to `exit`, all scratch restored), runs `C` once per occupied cell of a protected unary
clock tape and halts silently on the clock's blank. -/
def repeatTM (C : FinTM Bool) (entry exit : C.State) : FinTM Bool
/-- `N` bounded clean calls along the orbit of `f` complete in at most `N (B + 2) + 1` steps,
with the final state word `f^[N] s`; **every head stays within the source envelope plus the
clock tape `[0, N]`**.
**Proof sketch.** Induct on the executed clock prefix: each round is a tick, one relocated clean
call and a return dispatch. The envelope clause follows each call's envelope and the clock
head's monotone walk. -/
theorem repeatTM_complete …
```

The output, budget, argument and `clA5Iter_*` declarations stay in `Hardness` as the consumer
side.

**Net (est.).** Removed: at most 172 lines; the consumer half stays. Added:
- the moved 172
- re-expression without item 13: +20–60
- head-envelope and resource clauses, which are **new proofs** (no space fact exists today):
  +80–200
- docs, equations and module header: +70–110

That is **+170 to +370** net, with 0 pairs retired. Rule 10: the 14 members and 3 use sites read
`Cfg.ofWords`, `Cfg.workTapeSymbols`, `MultiTapeTM.step`, `Action.apply`, `stateWord`,
`seamCompTM` and `pairEncode` (by `simp`), plus `Fin.addCases` (a Mathlib definition passed to
`simp`). Their 23 `rfl`, 5 `change` and 8 `show` steps mostly read the clock configuration. Once
moved, every `clPlaced*`/`clKeepLastPlacement` read becomes foreign or must be rewritten.

**Statement changes:** none.

**Recommendation: carry** in the register as an accepted private host with one consumer.
Policy's harvest trigger is "before a second consumer is briefed", and none is.

**One lead could flip this.** If `ClassNP/PolyTimeBlockLoop` (or another public module) already
exports a polynomial *iteration closure*, then `clA5Iter_native` and `clA5Iter_shrinking` could
cite it. All 12 `clRepeat*` would become dead code, about −300 lines with no new API. That closure
would read: `PolyTimeComputable f`, `s`, and unary `N`, plus a polynomial orbit-size bound, imply
`PolyTimeComputable (fun x => f^[N x] (s x))`. The bundle only shows the `BlockLoop` orbit layer
(backlog BL-W), which looks ch7-specific. A one-line `git grep` settles it.

## 10. Method and limits

- **Extraction.** Bundle sections were split on their `## ===== path =====` headers. Lean bodies
  were taken between the code fences. Line numbers equal the file's own (checked against the
  plan's 4,370 and 8,701 and against 286 inventory entries).
- **Declarations.** A comment- and docstring-stripped column-0 header parse (modifiers,
  `def/lemma/theorem/abbrev/structure/instance`), with a namespace stack. A span ends at the next
  top-level item; trailing blanks are dropped.
- **Twins.** Exact means the comment-stripped code is equal after prefix normalization
  (`sat|Sat ↔ clA5|CLA5`). Near twins use a token `SequenceMatcher` ratio ≥ 0.80 over all
  SAT×Hardness pairs of at least 4 lines.
- **Use sites.** A word-boundary mention of a member's name in another declaration of the same
  file. All members are private, so no other file can mention them.
- **Read forms.** Counts of `rfl`, `change`, `show` and `decide` in proof text. The identifiers in
  `simp`/`simp only`/`simpa`/`dsimp`/`rw`/`unfold` argument lists were classified as same-file
  definitions, same-file lemmas, hypotheses, or other-file definition candidates, then checked by
  hand for the tables above.
- **Limits.** This does not see reads made by anonymous constructors, `obtain`, `exact`
  unification, or `dsimp only` with no arguments. The seal (sealed copy plus `rfl` controls) is the
  authority, and the repair counts above are lower bounds on the number of affected proofs.
- **Not measured.** Copy-screen pair counts, which need `copy-text-screen-v3.py` on the tree;
  replay closure sizes; imports' transitive reach.

# R4 design delivery: maintainer intake (2026-11-16)

**Delivery.** `r4-design.md` (51,083 bytes, SHA-256 `66a99292…95ce`), copied verbatim from the exchange
branch (`arora-barak-ch3-4/inbox/r4-design/r4-design.md`, exchange commit `3b5e3d4d7`). It was produced by a
Claude cloud worker from bundle `d8da8a45…` (Lean `68cba664`, records `4211cada`). No Lean was run. Treated
as data; the claims below were rechecked by the maintainer against the tree at `68cba664`.

## Rechecked and confirmed

- `clA5Compare_compute` cites `exists_first_entry_of_fixed` at `Hardness:7252`. The maintainer inventory's
  `7264` is wrong. Five more Hardness sites cite it: 1279, 1742, 2164, 3003, 3271.
- `sat_guard_add`/`clA5_guard_add` (`SAT:4035`/`Hardness:6368`) is an exact twin that is missing from the
  maintainer inventory. So is the SAT-side kind-4 instance `satScanTM/Cfg/_step/_run/_computes` (`SAT:230–301`).
  The inventory has no `guard_add` or `satScan` entry.
- Import reach (closure computed on the tree):
  - `SAT` reaches `Build/Loop` but not `Build/EmitIterEmbed`, `Build/WordTests`, `PolyTimeBlockLoop` or
    `BinaryArith/Iterate`.
  - `Hardness` reaches `EmitIterEmbed`, `WordTests` and `PolyTimeBlockLoop`, but not `Iterate`.
  - Neither `Iterate`'s closure nor `EmitIterEmbed`'s contains `SAT` or `Hardness`, so the imports below
    would create no cycle.
- `FinTM.computesFunInTime_decideEq` (PL-1's target) is in `Build/WordTests`, which imports only
  `Build/Primitives`.

## Maintainer additions (not in the delivery)

1. **K3 already has a public home.** `Build/EmitIterEmbed` publishes `padAction`, `embedCfg`,
   `embedCfg_ofWords`, `padAction_apply`, `embed_step` and `embed_run`. `satPad*`/`clA5Pad*` are its special
   case with an identity state map: the definitions match field for field.
   - K3 can therefore be retired as citations with **no new API**, separately from K6's host question.
   - `satPad_run` is unconditional, but `embed_run` takes an exit-avoidance hypothesis. The run lemma would
     come from `embed_step` plus `runFrom_comm_of_step` (est.).
   - Hardness needs no import. SAT needs `import …Build.EmitIterEmbed`, a new import into a frozen file.
2. **`guard_add` has a public counterpart.** `EmitIterEmbed.SafeRun.trans` states the same concatenation fact.
3. **The SG1-UH lead (delivery §4) is partly confirmed.**
   - `Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_iterate` (`ClassP/BinaryArith/Iterate.lean:190`) exists. It is
     public, built on `BlockLoop`, and needs only orbit-length bounds.
   - It is not a drop-in replacement: it fixes the iteration count at `a(|z|+1)^k`, whereas `clA5Iter_native`
     needs a count `N x` given in unary. A variable-count corollary is needed: a counter-guarded round
     iterated a polynomial number of times, using `PolyTimeComputable.output_length_le` to bound `N x`.
     Est. 50–110 lines.
   - `clVisitStep_native` exists, so `clVisitRows_native` can use the same closure.
   - The dead code would then be the 12 `clRepeat*` declarations, `clNative_cleanCall` and
     `clVisitStep_cleanCall`, whose only uses are the repeat path (`Hardness:5653`, `6042`, `6753`).
   - The SG1-UH lead changes from a host move costing an est. +170 to +370 lines to a private deletion of an
     est. −150 to −300 lines, with no new public API. It needs a new import into frozen `Hardness`
     (`ClassP/BinaryArith/Iterate`; cycle-free).
   - Measurement needed before any ruling. It would also remove 5 of item 13's 42 use sites.

## ===== campaign/duplication-ledger.md =====

# Cumulative duplication ledger

The standing per-file accounting of copied proved material that
`workflow.md` §4 requires at every epoch boundary. Created as the
retrofit-R1 round-1 repair (R1-2); **rebuilt at round 2** (R2-1/R2-2 of
`audits/retrofit-r1-r2-findings.md`): the first version's arithmetic was
inconsistent (summands 261 against a printed 249), its inclusion rule was
applied asymmetrically, and it **misclassified an exact three-file copy
family as "design-harvest reimplementation"** — the round-2 auditor
proved the four relocation declarations byte-identical across `Loop`,
`Primitives`, and `Hardness` after consistent identifier substitution,
and found the 13 exact Loop-internal H3 copies omitted. This version
adopts one inclusion rule, enumerates every family, and uses the
auditor's independently computed figures wherever they exist.

## Counting convention (one rule)

**Primary rule — expanded correspondence membership**: a declaration is a
ledger member iff it belongs to a *recorded cross-declaration
correspondence* — the retrofit inventories' twin maps **including their
strengthened-counterpart rows**, the A2/F2A reports' declared copies, and
the round-2 audit's verified relocation and H3 families. Each member is
counted **once per file it inhabits**. (Secondary, where it differs: the
*strict normalized-byte-twin* count excludes the five strengthened
counterparts — Loop's `loopHost_prepare`/`loopHost_contracts`,
Primitives' `splitSolve_of_body`/`_source`/`_closed` — and H3's one
near-copy `_init` pair.) Fractions are members over the file's total
declarations. Line figures use the round-2 audit's span rule — attached
docstring and intervening closure note through the last code line,
excluding separating blank/module-note blocks — with the auditor's
computed values where available and estimates under the same rule marked
`≈`.

**The public-proof screen (round-5 repair of R4-1; R5-1/R5-2/R5-3).**
Published as `audits/evidence/retrofit/r1-public-proof-screen.py` with its
output `r1-public-proof-screen.out`. *Erratum:* the round-4 run tested
whether a source proof was contained **whole** in its counterpart, but the
round-4 text described "segments ≥ 60 characters". The round-5 auditor ran
the method as described and found six fragment hits that the containment
test could not see. The method below is the one actually run.

- **Method.** Strip comments and all whitespace. Rename each source
  identifier `h` to `f2_h` wherever Catalog declares `f2_h` (dotted names
  split). Report two measures:
  - the **longest common contiguous segment** (LCS), with the literal ≥ 60
    candidate threshold;
  - the **shared length**: greedy string tiling with blocks of at least 25
    characters, as a fraction of the **source** proof.
- **Rule.** A pair is a **member** when at least half of the source proof
  reappears in the target, with an absolute floor of 60 shared characters
  so that a one-line citation of a public lemma counts as reuse. Any other
  shared tiling of at least 60 characters is a recorded **fragment**, not
  counted. The rest are citations or no match.
- **Population (R5-3).** 17 eligible pairs: 2 from Composition (`id`,
  `const`) and **15** from Primitives, not the 16 stated in round 4. Five
  source theorems have no `_spaceUsed` counterpart: `ifEq`, `comp`,
  `splitSolveWith`, `unaryToken`, `appendBit`.
- **Pass 1, direct pairs.**
  - Members (7): `id` 96.5%, `const` 97.1%, `prepend` 93.9%,
    `pairEncodeFixed` 100%, `pairFst`/`pairSnd` 88.8%, `pairConcat`
    88.7%.
  - Fragments, recorded and not counted (3): `polyUnary` (119 characters
    shared, 46.7%); `pairLenCheck` (305, 21.9%; its LCS is the 91-character
    `Nat.pow_one` bound); `stripLast` (221, 11.7%; its LCS is the
    121-character `have hn` weakening).
  - Citations or no match (7): `lengthBits`, `polyBits`, `pairValid`,
    `pairDup`, `pairMapSnd`, `splitSolve` (the auditor's 27-character
    citation), `incFixed`.
  - The literal ≥ 60 LCS screen reproduces the auditor's hit set exactly
    (`id` 776, `const` 273, and 62/75/75/75/91/121 for the six Primitives
    pairs). One member falls below the 60-character LCS threshold:
    `pairEncodeFixed`, whose longest block is 53 characters but whose whole
    91-character source proof reappears. This is why the rule measures
    coverage, not contiguity alone.
- **Pass 2, residual helpers.** Each of the 27 nonmembers recorded in
  round 4 is screened against every public proof of Composition,
  Primitives and TimeConstructible, taking the best match by shared length.
  - Members (2): `f2_strip_linear` (86.0% of `computesFunInTime_stripLast`;
    R5-1) and `f2_counter_heads` (64.1% of `timeConstructible_id`; the
    auditor's 215-character partial-reuse candidate, which crosses the
    member bar once measured by tiling).
  - Fragments, recorded (6): `f2_counter_count_space` 6.5%,
    `f2_unary_sharp` 35.7%, `f2_cond_time` 30.0% (vs
    `bufferedCompTM_computesInTime`, a candidate the auditor did not list),
    `f2_rewind_scan_heads` 7.4%, `f2_rewind_heads` 6.0%,
    `f2_cond_ledger` 11.7%.
  - The remaining 19 share under 60 characters with any public proof.
- **Round-6 repair (R6-1, R6-5): pass 3, exhaustive.** Round 6 found
  R6-1, which the public-only residual pass could not see. Pass 3 replaces
  that scope limit. **Every one of Catalog's 124 non-members** (all of
  Catalog minus the post-R6-1 299-member union, computed by name in the
  script) is screened against **every declaration, public and private, of
  Composition, Primitives, TimeConstructible, Loop and Wrappers** (553
  declarations, of which 542 have an extracted body of at least 25
  characters; the other 11 cannot reach the 60-character floor). An exact 25-character prefilter is used; it loses nothing,
  because every tile is at least 25 characters. Verdicts compare like with
  like, proof with proof and term with term, so a proof that spells out a
  definition's term is reported as a restatement and not counted. **Every**
  qualifying pair is printed, not just each target's best match (R6-5).
  - Result: **19 cross-file members**, all counted in the Catalog row
    above. *Round-7 correction:* the round-6 text derived the source side
    from each target's best match only, giving "6 new source-side members"
    (R7-1). Pass 4 below replaces that hand step.
  - Five A2 members reproduce just over half of one 129-character Loop
    proof, `emLoop_run_prefix`. They are counted, as the rule requires,
    and flagged as low-coverage.
- **Round-7 repair (R7-1, R7-2): pass 4 generates the census.** No
  per-file member count is assembled by hand any more. **Pass 4** runs the
  like-kind rule over **all 423 Catalog declarations**, not only the
  non-members, against all five source files: 537 like-kind MEMBER pairs.
  **Every** pair's source joins its file's member set, together with the
  historical rules, stated by name in the script: f2_-twins, the
  `a2_loop_halted_run` twin, the relocation family, the 13 H3 copies, the
  counter block and `catalog_` twins. The script prints each file's count
  and every member beyond the historical rules, with spans. The rows above
  quote it.
  - Pass 4 reproduces the auditor's R7-1 additions (`controlCfg_run`,
    `emCall_right_run`, `exists_emitLoopTM`).
  - It also finds **24 further source-side members** (Primitives 16, Loop
    7, Wrappers 1). These are source declarations that a Catalog twin of a
    *sibling* declaration reproduces by more than half, so their material
    is duplicated in Catalog. Two of them are Loop's H3 near-copies
    `emLoopHost_init` and `emLoopHost_anchor_return`, previously
    "noted, uncounted"; they are now counted through the cross-file path.
  - Catalog is unchanged at 318.
  - **R7-2:** the body extractor now handles equation-style definitions and
    inductives (text from the first depth-0 `|` or `where`). The population
    labels are exact: 553 source declarations, 542 with an extracted body
    of at least 25 characters; the other 11 are genuinely shorter. Pass 3b
    carries the kind guard: **107 like-kind in-file pairs over 62 targets
    (12 at 90% or more), plus 2 restatements** (`f2_cond_ledger` ~
    `f2_timedReadyCfg`, `a2_loop_prepare` ~ `f2_loopReady`).
- **The membership rule in one sentence.** A declaration is a member when
  it is a historical twin or copy, or when it is either side of a
  like-kind cross-file pair in which at least half of the source's
  extracted body, and at least 60 characters, reappears in the target. The
  **exception** is in-file near-duplicates, which are recorded (pass 3b)
  and not counted; in-file exact copies are counted.
- **Standing in-file convention, stated explicitly.** Pass 3b lists
  in-file near-duplicates among the non-members: **109 raw printed
  pairs, of which 107 are like-kind, over 62 targets**. Twelve like-kind
  pairs reach 90%, and the other 2 are kind-mismatched restatements. They
  are led by the §12 sibling
  machine rows (`transferTM` against `copyTM` 99.8%, and the
  clear/compare/increment rows), which are public constructions audited at
  the §12 and F1 gates. Per the ledger's standing convention, which counts
  in-file **exact** copies (the H3 thirteen, the `a2_mapSumEquiv`/
  `a2_map_sum` pair) and **notes in-file near-duplicates without counting
  them**, they are recorded, not counted. None is an exact copy. Their
  disposition is the 12.2c per-theme split, which factors these families.
  An in-file near-match alone never adds a member. A declaration can still
  be a member independently through a cross-file pair: Loop's
  `emLoopHost_init` and `emLoopHost_anchor_return` count because their
  Catalog twins reproduce them.
- **Coverage qualification.** The screen covers the five source files of
  Catalog's copy families, in full, at the stated thresholds. Copies from
  files outside those families, or adaptations restructured below the
  25-character tile size, are outside it.

Copy-side counts deliberately include copies whose originals were deleted
in R1 (the copies persist; deletion of an original does not shrink the
copy side). The Loop inventory's recorded dispositions — the 8 dead
Loop-twin copies in Catalog (`f2_loop_silent_prefix`,
`f2_loopBody_capture`, the six `f2_loopDebit*`/`f2_loopBorrow*`) and the
orphans' dead twins — are **dispositions for 12.2c, not subtractions
here**; sole-owner/dead labels require Catalog's reference graph and are
settled at that window. Internal near-duplicates flagged by the
inventories but outside the rule (`clCountTape ≡ bufferTape`) are noted,
uncounted. The H3 `_init` pair, once in this list, counts since round 7
through its cross-file Catalog correspondence.

**SAT/Hardness adapter debt (gate106 F2; ACKNOWLEDGED by kind by Seyoon, 2026-11-07).**
The acknowledgment covers every re-derivation of the following generic kinds anywhere in
TCSlib, including matching correctness/frame proofs, not merely the currently found sites:

1. **Clean-module contract and its install/emit/stop lifting:** a positive bounded first halt
   from canonical argument tapes, uniform in untouched native input, with prescribed result
   word and emitted output. Canonical current formula is SatClean/CLA5Clean.
2. **Positive-release stop adapter:** add a Boolean release flag so a designated exit becomes
   a halt only after the first source step; preserve physical configuration fields. Includes
   the machine/configuration, step and clean-contract lemmas.
3. **Bank-padding adapter:** embed a k-tape action/configuration/machine into K≥k tapes with
   unused tapes blank, heads0 and stationary actions; includes apply/run/seam commutation.
4. **Finite one-way word transducer:** zero work tapes, parametric finite next/emit/finish/start,
   at most one emission per input plus optional final emission. Includes pure word semantics,
   configuration, run, polynomial-time and head/tail projection proofs.
5. **Polynomial bridge overhead:** len≤A(n+1)^d implies
   c*(A(n+1)^d+n+len+1)+1≤(c*(2*A+1)+1)*(n+1)^(d+1).

Independent full-header/code comparison found22 exact prefix-renaming pairs,298 declaration
span lines in each file: clean4, padding6, release-stop4, transducer7, bridge1. These extend
the auditor's seven-pair lower bound; they are not raw screen-edge counts.

**PL-1, the linear-to-polynomial lift, and WT-1's residue** (PR #171, the word tests, 2026-10-27;

  (`ClassNP/PolyTimePairing`, lines 64 and 71). `Nondeterminism` does not import `PolyTimePairing`;

- `Savitch`'s inline `hD'` (`SpaceComplexity/Savitch`, line 193 in `spaceConstructible_poly`'s
  proof): the conversion of `computesFunInTime_ifEq [] [true] [false]` to `[decide (x = [])]`,

  user's D1 (A) licensed this leaf; the v3 screen pairs it with the first at 61%.

#172's head `33d68537`, a tree before #171): `Nondeterminism` 1 of 201 (8 public, 193 private; 0.5%;

**LS-2, the logarithmic bound by the binary length** (gate 89, round 4's search; ruled with it, user,
2026-11-04: "Fix in #181 now"). The fact is `logSpace n ≤ Nat.size n + 1`, equivalently
`≤ |bits n| + 1`; its converse is `|bits n| ≤ Nat.log 2 n + 1`. Before round 4:
- the public `Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.logSpace_le_size_succ` (`Logspace/ISCountMath`);
- inline re-derivations in `Randomized/BPLInP`, twice (`two_pow_codes_le`, `BPL_subset_P`);
- the public `Randomized.PolyAmp.logSpace_le_ell` (`Randomized/SpaceAmplifyPoly`, its `ell n` is
  `|bits n| + 1`), re-proved through `Nat.log_lt_of_lt_pow`;
- the converse, published as `LogProg.length_bits_le_log` (`Machines/Bin`) and re-derived by the
  private `size_le_logSpace` (`Logspace/ISCountGenCorrect`).

All in Hydroxyi's files. `BPLInP` did not import `ISCountMath`. **Retired by #181, round 4**
(`fe4bdb67`, `227d92ee`): `logSpace_le_size_succ` moves verbatim to `SpaceComplexity/Basic` as
`Complexity.logSpace_le_size_succ`, and the four re-derivations cite it or `length_bits_le_log`
(copy deletions and re-points, FYI). Same round, same ruling: `ExpBFS/Run`'s `setup_run` cites its
own file's `lgv_le_succ` for `hv |x| ≤ |x|` instead of re-deriving it (`252bbcb8`).

**CL-1, the codec languages' sibling idiom** (gate 91, the edge-mode PR's screen; ruled with it,
user, 2026-11-04). Each code language of `SpaceComplexity/Codec` has its own definition, its own
membership lemma at an encoded input (`mem_validLang`, …), its own characterization through the
word-level check (`validLang_iff`, …) and its own decider proof (`validLang_mem`, …). The proofs
repeat two pieces: the decoding of `⟨x, ⟨bits c, bits s⟩⟩` (`pairEncode_inj` twice, then
`bits_injective`) and the decider wrapper (`arm_decides_poly` on `CA`, the `one_run` case split and
the reject branch). The four languages `validLang`, `initLang`, `acceptLang` and `stepLang`
(Hydroxyi's) already formed 31 copy pairs at the base. The edge-mode PR adds `edgeLang`,
`mem_edgeLang`, `edgeLang_iff` and `edgeLang_mem`, 25 more pairs. About 25 lines of shared text
are the decoding proofs and the wrapper's skeleton. The edge mode's own correctness proof
(`edge_round`, `edge_loop`, `edge_tail`) is in no pair. **Census** (gate 91, minor 3; members of the
family over all declarations, private included): `Langs` 8/9 → 10/12, `Checks` 4/26 → 5/31,
`Deciders` 3/16 → 4/22. `Langs` was already above one fifth at the base, from the four existing
languages; the acceptance above covers it. The edge member crosses no new file's threshold.
**Accepted (user, 2026-11-04)** as debt. **Disposition:** the dedup window (12.2c): one membership
lemma for languages of encoded triples, and one decider wrapper parameterized by the mode's tail,
with the five languages re-proved through them. This reworks Hydroxyi's proved deciders, interface
design that waits for him. **Ruled (the user, 2026-11-06; Hydroxyi not active): the full refactor.** **Retired: #220 merged 2026-11-07 (`b9855020`); gate 111; follow-up CK-1.**

one of its steps repeated `ExpBFS.inWin_mono`'s second component verbatim. The v3 screen paired

  public as `Turing.Cfg.InWindow.apply_iff`, over any alphabet, beside the new
  `Turing.Cfg.InWindow.mono`; `apply_of_lt` is proved from the two; and the record step
  (`recordStep_observed_action`), the private lemma's one use, cites `apply_iff`.
- **The family, acknowledged by kind for 12.2c (user, 2026-11-05), widened by kind (user,
  2026-11-05):** every proof, anywhere in TCSlib, that one step keeps a configuration within a
  window of any shape (the radius window `Cfg.InWindow`, a per-tape radius, an interval, a
  visited interval), and every proof of window monotonicity. A later find is an accounting minor.
  The canonical statements:
  - `Turing.Cfg.InWindow.apply_iff`: for `c` in the radius-`s` window, `(a.apply c).InWindow s`
    holds iff no work head is at `-s` moving left or at `s` moving right;
  - `Turing.Cfg.InWindow.mono`: `c.InWindow s → s ≤ s' → c.InWindow s'`;
  - **the tape half**, to be published in the 12.2c window: an action changes a work cell only
    under that tape's old head (`z ≠ c.workTapePos i → (a.apply c).workTapes i z =
    c.workTapes i z`). It exists today as `TuringMachine/Oracle`'s private
    `apply_workTapes_eq_of_ne` (line 304 at the campaign tip), the natural one to harvest.
- **Members on `Cfg.InWindow`** (lines at the campaign tip):
  - `Complexity.ExpBFS.inWin_mono` and `inWin_stepWith` (`SpaceComplexity/ExpBFS/Radius`, lines
    63 and 70; Hydroxyi's): the monotonicity, and one choice step from radius `s` into `s + 1`;
  - the window half of `Complexity.Codec.boundary_iff` (`SpaceComplexity/Codec/Step`, line 195;
    Hydroxyi's): once the two boundary cells are read as head conditions, `apply_iff`;
  - `codec_step_blank` (private, `ClassPSPACE/TQBF`, line 1505; the campaign's): the tape half at

## ===== campaign/backlog.md =====

# Backlog

The consolidated tracking file for the Arora-Barak campaign branch
(`complexity/arora-barak-ch1`) and adjacent repository work: human-review
design questions, queued and on-hold campaign work, deferred formalizations,
pending decisions, and housekeeping. Consolidated 2026-09-18 from the two
campaign plans, the audit resolutions records, and session assessments.

**Conventions.** This file is the *canonical home* of the human-review
question statements (§1) — the plans keep stable numbered stubs, since audit
documents cite the numbering — and the *tracking index* for everything else
(scope prose remains in the plans; decision-log history is never moved).
New items land here; an item leaves only by a decision recorded in the
relevant plan's decision log. From the next audit round onward this file
joins the bundle attachment set.

---

## 1. Human-review design questions (reserved — never closed by an automated gate)

Flagged for a **human** auditor/maintainer: the LLM audit rounds verify
correctness, but these are matters of architectural taste and trust-surface
policy.

### CH1-Q1 — the 3A Mathlib-computability bridge

*Origin: `AroraBarakChapter1Plan.md` §5 (epoch 3, batch A);
`MathlibBridge.lean`, `Turing.exists_effectiveMachineCode`.*

The audited docstring sketch called for the canonizer machine to be
**hand-assembled from this repository's composition combinators** ("its
construction uses the composition combinators", optionally with a polynomial
`canonizerTime`). The delivered proof instead (i) proves the canonization
*function* primitive recursive, (ii) compiles it through **Mathlib's verified
recursion-theory pipeline** (`ToPartrec.Code.exists_code` →
`PartrecToTM2.tr_eval`), (iii) simulates the resulting TM2 stack machine in
our model with a bespoke private `bridgeTM`, and (iv) lands in the binary
alphabet via the proved `alphabet_reduction`, extracting the time bound by
finite maxima (no polynomial bound claimed — permitted, since
`canonizerTime` is existential). The batch flagged the deviation itself; the
maintainer verification pass confirmed the proof is sorry-free with the
standard axiom footprint and zero public-interface drift. **Open questions
for a human:** (a) is the heavyweight `Mathlib.Computability.TMToPartrec`
import into the TM tree acceptable, or should the bridge be quarantined
behind the planned phase-5 `MathlibBridge` module boundary (it effectively
front-runs that module)? (b) is the enlarged trust/review surface (Mathlib's
TM2 semantics + the private `bridgeTM` simulation, ~150 private
declarations) preferable to a longer but self-contained combinator
construction? (c) should the abandoned polynomial-`canonizerTime` claim be
recorded as permanently out of scope, or re-derived later from the
combinator route if one is ever written? Since the epoch-3→4 merge the
bridge lives in the dedicated `MathlibBridge.lean`, which implements the
quarantine that part (a) contemplates — the `TMToPartrec` import is confined
to that one module and nothing outside `exists_effectiveMachineCode` depends
on it — but the implemented quarantine does **not** dispose of this
question: parts (a)-(c) remain open for human review (epoch-4 audit,
finding 3: an earlier version of this text misplaced the bridge inside
`Encoding.lean`).

*Cross-link: part (c) gained relevance in Chapter 2 — see §3, "Polynomial
canonizer for a concrete scheme".*

### CH1-Q2 — the 3B universal-interpreter proof architecture

*Origin: `AroraBarakChapter1Plan.md` §5 (epoch 3, batches B + B2);
`Universal.lean`, `Turing.universal`.*

The proof followed the audited sketch's outline (prefix-only startup,
canonizer capture onto a table tape, four-work-tape interpreter with a fixed
finite controller), but the realized architecture is by far the campaign's
most involved artifact: 2465 lines (2831 after the epoch-4A timed fill), 104
private declarations built across two agent sessions (WIP `f191b918` +
continuation), a bespoke checkpoint relation (`universalRelation`) with
generic block-simulation assembly (`universal_block_run` /
`universal_from_blocks`), a virtual left boundary via a marker tape, a unary
state tape with group-wise table scanning, and an *exact* per-phase cost
ledger realized to `universalBlockBound = 3L + 5N + 20`. The kernel checks
all of it, and the public statement is frozen and audited — but the *design*
was never itself an audit deliverable at this level of detail. **Open
questions for a human:** (a) is this the right load-bearing shape — and
which parts (the capture wrapper, the block-run/`universal_run_join`
assembly, the marker-directed rewind and unary-copy gadget patterns, all
flagged by the agents as promotion candidates) should graduate to shared
modules rather than being re-derived? (b) is the exact-ledger posture
(`3L + 5N + 20` proved to the transition) worth its brittleness against any
future change to `CodeTM.serialize`, or should the maintained invariant be
an existential bound with the exact ledger demoted to documentation? (c)
does the interpreter's claim to *be* the book's universal machine (as
opposed to satisfying the frozen statement, which the kernel settles)
deserve a targeted human read of the construction's core definitions
(`UniversalControl`, `universalInterpreter`, `universalRelation`), given no
executable diagnostics of the whole interpreter ever ran (the batch-B smoke
tests aborted on deep recursion and were discarded)?

*Cross-link: question (b)'s exact ledger is now also load-bearing for the
Chapter-2 `TMSAT_mem_NP` fill (the quantitative public bridge, §2), which
will expose a form of the constant publicly.*

### CH2-Q1 — generality of `HALT_not_mem_NP`

*Origin: `AroraBarakChapter2Plan.md` (phase-1, round-2 audit, finding 3);
`ClassNP/Reductions.lean`.*

The statement is currently at `Turing.EffectiveMachineCode` generality
because its proof route reuses Chapter 1's `HALT_not_computable`, whose own
proof runs the universal evaluator. The round-2 auditor showed this
restriction is **not mathematically necessary**: a direct diagonalization —
the public diagonal-pairing machine, the searcher's finite-control transform
with the halt/loop roles swapped, `Turing.exists_codeTM`, no evaluator —
proves `HALT` undecidable for *every* lawful `Turing.MachineCode` (and the
earlier "trivial-machine scheme" counterexample is unlawful: constant
decoding violates `decode_encode`). **The question:** add that diagonal
lemma as a new audited statement (a strengthening of Chapter 1's
uncomputability story that shares its main fill obligation, the
control-transform lemma, with `HALT_NPHard`) and generalize
`HALT_not_mem_NP` to `MachineCode` — or keep the conservative signature as a
documented API/proof-route restriction? Maintainer's provisional choice,
pending review: the conservative signature, with the docstring stating the
restriction honestly; the diagonal lemma is deliberately *not* slipped into
a repair round, since it would enlarge the audited surface of Chapter 1's
uncomputability chapter.

---

### CH7-D1 — the block stack's per-loop lemma family (duplication threshold crossed)

*Origin: the ch7 fill gate, run on the merged ch3-4 tree after PR #11

### U-1: re-derive the chapter-1 universal machine from B5a's generic step block (user, 2026-10-11)

*Merged with MIG-2 (user, 2026-10-12): the timed-layer dedup and this re-derivation are one migration item.*

The chapter-1 universal machine (`Turing.universal`, `universal_quadratic`, `timed_universal`) is
a bespoke interpreter of about 5,300 lines across `Universal.lean`, `UniversalStartup.lean`,
`UniversalInterpreter.lean` and `UniversalBlock.lean`. It is hard-wired to one work tape, and it
is already copied once: the timed form carries its own private stopped-interpreter layer. B5a
(`briefs/b5a-fill.md`, design §12.11) builds one format-parameterized interpreter instead. That
is a single private step block for one simulated transition of a `k`-tape coded table, whose
per-round cost is independent of `t` and `x`.

**The item:** after B5a lands, re-derive the three chapter-1 statements from that step block, and
delete the bespoke interpreter layers.

**H1 alone does not suffice.** The frozen statements need what B5a's headline does not give:
- **full output:** `universal` computes `M_α(x)`, and `timed_universal` emits `true :: output`,
  whereas H1 answers only `[true]`/`[false]` from a silent output summary;
- **a per-code linear bound with no `|x|` term:** `universal` is `C(α)·(t + 1)` and
  `timed_universal` is `C(α)·(t + 1)²`, whereas H1 is a polynomial in `|α| + |x| + t`;
- **no deadline, and divergence preserved:** `universal` runs until halt, and its converse says
  every completed output of `U` is one of the simulated machine's.

**Route.** Reuse the step block under new hosts. The natural route is H2 above (the per-code
linear timed simulator, with its suffix-input host), plus an emitting variant of the block's
output handling and an unclocked loop host for `universal`. Keep all three statements unchanged;
`UniversalStartup`'s public input pieces (`universalInput_read`/`_move`) are the suffix-input
host's components.

**Governance.** A 12.2c item: its own PR and gate. The chapter-1 statements are frozen, and every
consumer of `universal`/`timed_universal` is re-checked. Prerequisite: the B5a fill (H1's step
block proved). *Origin: B5a design discussion; user, 2026-10-11.*

### SH-1: retire `Nondeterminism`'s private 2B shell onto W2-V (from the fills-4 integration)

`FinTM.exists_certificateShell` (W2-V, `Build/CertShell.lean`) is proved and admission-free. It
is the public form of the private certificate shell that `ClassNP/Nondeterminism.lean` uses for
`ntime_poly_subset_NP` (`cont_choiceVerifier_mem_P`, its loader, `choiceCore`). Design §12.10,
decision 3, names the deduplication as the shell's second customer, a 12.2c item. W2-V's

90%. This is one four-line `match` term, the output function of the public
`FinTM.computesFunInTime_splitSolve`, and it was pre-disclosed by W2-V's brief
(`audits/fills-4-integration.md`).

**Scope (corrected 2026-10-12, from the 12.2c readiness check).** W2-V's shell serves only
*polynomial* certificate lengths, so only the polynomial use retires. `Nondeterminism`'s NEXP
route keeps its own exponential search: `e3Split` solves `n + C·2^((n+1)^c) = m`, and its loader
reuses `contPairTM`, which embeds `choiceCore`. **The task, as scoped:** re-derive
`cont_choiceVerifier_mem_P` from `exists_certificateShell` and delete `contSplitWord` with it,
which retires the 100% pair. `e3SplitWord`, `contPairTM` and `choiceCore` stay for the
exponential route. Retiring those too would need a width-parametric public shell: a new
statement, with its own gate, and not worth it for the remaining 90% textual match. Statements
stay unchanged. **Prerequisite:** W2-V's own fill gate (the wave-1 fill gate), so that the cited
shell is audited first. The task gets its own PR and gate.

- **stmt:** new public statements, so a statement gate;
- **full:** retired or changed statements, so a full gate, with the consumers edited in the same PR.

* **PROG-2: the extension edit set** (user, 2026-10-12; design §15c). All four extensions in one
  scripted vendored edit set:
  - `inBit`/`inLen` with a RAM `rdIn` (`len` only if needed);
  - `emit`, with an append-only output;
  - read-once coins (`coin x`);
  - `half`, as a statement and a RAM shift.

  I/O and coins become indices of `Exec`, so `Ends`, `Meets` and the routines are unchanged; a new
  `EndsIO` sees them. Also part of the set:
  - the `Exec` determinism lemma, which randomized acceptance needs;
  - `Fits`'s input-length clause;
  - an update to `ComputationalModels.lean`'s instruction-count docstring.

  **Estimate:** 600–1,000 vendored lines, by `scripts/vendor_afm26/`, plus 700–1,150 new.
  **Gate:** a fidelity check of the vendored edits, then a statement gate for the new rules.
  **Obligation from the stage-2 gate (F3):** the edited compiler must supply `1 ≤ lim.word` at the
  existing simulation calls (`Compiler/Simulation.lean:277`, `:356`), as an invariant or a
  premise; it does not follow from `input_le`.

* **PROG-3: memory footprint along a run** (from the PROG-2 survey; design §15c, obstacle 1).
  `compileProgram_correct` describes only the final memory. Stage 2's space bound needs every
  intermediate memory inside `[-lowCell, lim.space)`. Close it with a stronger `Steps` or by
  porting `Machine/Footprint.lean` (PROG-1(e)). It is a prerequisite for stage 2's space bound,
  and so for L, Savitch and PSPACE through programs, and for C2's log-space programs (design
  §16b item 4).

* **PROG-4: stage 2's statement requirements** (user, 2026-10-12; design §16b items 1 and 4).
  Stage 2 (PROG-1(d)) is drafted together with PROG-2 and PROG-3, and its statement carries:
  - **a computed word size:** `W` is a function of the input length that the compiled machine
    computes within its space bound (`c·log n` for P and L, `c·S(n)` for Savitch);
  - **deterministic and nondeterministic forms:** each `coin` one `FinNDTM` choice step, with
    bounds uniform over the coin streams;
  - **a logspace grade:** `O(1)` cells and `W = O(log n)` give space `O(log n)`.

  **Gate:** a statement gate, before any fill. **Drafted (2026-10-12; design §15d):** the
  statement drafts and notes are in `audits/evidence/stage2/`. **Answered (user, 2026-10-12):**
  all four as recommended (design §15d). **Statement gate (2026-10-13):**
  `audits/stage2-statements-pack.md`, covering PROG-2 (as a specification mirror), PROG-3 and
  PROG-4. **Gate CLOSED** (round 1, 2026-10-14: 0 blockers / 0 majors / 4 minors;
  `audits/stage2-statements-findings.md`, resolutions `audits/stage2-statements-resolutions.md`).
  No theorem is false; the homes, the namespace and `initMem` are approved. Next: the landing PR
  (parts A, C, D, E and the slice lemmas), then PROG-2's scripted edit and its fidelity gate.
  **Landed** (PR #86). **Paused (user, 2026-10-14):** the ARM merge proves PSPACE = NPSPACE,
  `PATH ∈ NL` and NL = coNL, the customers of the coin programs and of Savitch at polynomial
  space; general `savitch` stays sorried. No stage-2 brief (PROG-2's edit and fidelity gate,
  PROG-4's fills) is written until the user resumes it.

* **Machine-routine layer (user decision 2026-10-06: build once
  chapter 2 is done, in the E5-closure/D7 window, before chapter 3).**
  Three pieces, sized by the A-chain's evidence (≈ half of the A2/A3
  deliveries' 202 native privates are hand-rebuilt universal routines;
  `emitterBank*`/`emitterP2*` relocation privately re-harvested three
  times; A3's proved costs `3|w|+3` copy / `2|w|+2` clear match the
  prior art's `3w+2`/`2w+2` to within one step):
  1. a generic **bank-embedding theorem** — a verified routine on its
     own small tape set runs on any selected tape subset of a `k`-tape
     machine, cost unchanged, all other tapes/heads framed (the public
     generic form of `emitterBank*`/`clBank*`/`clSlot*`);
  2. a generic **seam-composition lemma** — sequential composition of
     two controllers at a canonical `Cfg.ofWords` seam with first-return
     cuts and additive budgets (the generic form of the per-batch
     dispatch gluing);
  3. **catalog promotion** of transfer/clear/copy/compare/increment as
     public machines with exact costs, seeded from the already-audited
     A-chain privates (D6-style promotion, not new proof work).
  **Survey update 2026-10-06 (pre-§12, recorded ahead of the
  colleague meeting 2026-10-07)**: the colleague's ch6 merge already
  supplies the **function-level half** of this layer —
  `TuringMachine/CounterProg{,Run}` (goto programs over unary
  registers, compiled once into `FinTM`, `t` abstract steps ≤
  `t(2t+3)` machine steps, FP bridge), `ClassNP/Transducer` (Mealy
  machines as work-tape-free FinTMs in `|x|+1`), `ClassNP/
  PolyTimePairing`/`PClosure` (FP/`P` closure, built ON our audited
  catalog), `UnaryTape`. The §12 design must **consume, not
  duplicate** these; the remaining gap is the **config-level half**
  (bank-embedding, seam-composition at canonical `Cfg.ofWords`
  seams — the emitter r1 finding stands: function contracts cannot
  deliver clean-return seams) plus residual catalog promotions.
  Items for the meeting: colleague roadmap (more campaign-module
  rewiring?), `CounterProg` as general substrate vs. sibling
  module, `Build/*` ownership during the retrofit window, ch3/
  TimeHierarchy alignment. Citation duty now extends to the
  colleague's modules alongside lax-434930.
  Mechanism: a design addendum (`machine-library-design.md` §12) →

  `d · (|α| + 1)^d · (t + 1)`, with no `|x|` term and linear in `t` per
  code. It would make the one interpreter the stage-1 timed universal at
  linear overhead. It needs a **suffix-input host**: the simulated machine
  reads `x` in place inside the native input, behind a left-boundary
  marker. The pieces are public (`universalInput_read`/`_move`,
  `UniversalStartup.lean`), but no host composes them. H2 ⇒ H1 is already
  proved (`exists_uniformSimulator_of_timed`, B5a statement probe), so H2
  can later be added beside H1 without disturbing its consumers. The step
  block's per-round cost is independent of `t` and `x`, so the B5a fill's
  trace is the H2 core. H2 is also the natural route for 12.2c item **U-1** (§1).

### Chapter 6 (Arora–Barak §§6.1–6.5): what is proved, and what remains

The machine-facing Chapter-6 bridge theorems this section used to list are all
**proved, sorry-free** (headline `#print axioms`: `propext`, `Classical.choice`,
`Quot.sound` only), over the book's DAG model `BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit`:

* Thm 6.6 `P ⊆ P/poly` — `Complexity.P_subset_PPoly` (oblivious tableau,
  `CircuitComplexity/PSubsetPPoly*.lean`); `P ⊊ P/poly` (p. 110) —
  `Complexity.P_ssubset_PPoly`, with the machine-model `UHALT`
  (`Complexity.UHALT_not_mem_P`, `UHaltMachine.lean`).
* Lem 6.10 / 6.11 — `BoolCircuit.dagCktSatLang_NPComplete`,
  `BoolCircuit.dagCktSatLang_polyTimeReducible_SAT3`, and Cook–Levin via circuits
  `Complexity.SAT3_NPHard_viaCircuits` (the p. 111 alternative proof); CKT-SAT `∈ NP` is
  `BoolCircuit.dagCktSatLang_mem_NP`, circuit evaluation `BoolCircuit.CVAL_mem_P`.
* Remark 6.7, Thm 6.13 — `Complexity.tabFamily_isPUniform`,
  `Language.mem_P_iff_exists_isPUniform`; Def 6.14, Thm 6.15 and the logspace half of
  Remark 6.7 — `Complexity.tabFamily_isLogspaceUniform`,
  `Language.mem_P_iff_exists_isLogspaceUniform`.
* Def 6.16, Ex 6.17, Thm 6.18 — `Complexity.DTIMEAdvice`,
  `Complexity.mem_PAdvicePoly_of_le_allOnes` (with the named `UHALT` instances
  `Complexity.UHALT_mem_DTIMEAdvice_one`, `Complexity.UHALT_mem_PAdvicePoly`),
  `Complexity.PPoly_eq_PAdvicePoly`, and the book's advice length `n^d` literally:
  `Complexity.PPoly_eq_iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_pow` (`P/poly = ⋃ DTIME(n^c + 1)/n^d`,
  `PAdviceSubsetPPoly.lean`). The time `n^c + 1` is forced, not cosmetic: the literal
  `DTIME(n^c)/a` is empty for `c ≥ 1` (`Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_pow_eq_empty`, zero steps
  on the empty input), so the literal union collapses to constant time
  (`Complexity.iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_pow_eq`); also
  `DTIME(T)/0 = DTIME(T)` for `T(n) ≥ n + 1` (`Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_DTIME`)
  and `⋃_c DTIME(n^c + 1)/0 = P` (`Complexity.iUnion_DTIMEAdvice_zero_eq_P`).
* Thm 6.19 Karp–Lipton — `Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_two_of_NP_subset_PPoly`; Thm 6.20
  Meyer — `Complexity.EXP_eq_SigmaP_two_of_EXP_subset_PPoly`, and the p. 115 corollary
  `Complexity.not_EXP_subset_PPoly_of_P_eq_NP`.
* Thm 6.21 — `BoolCircuit.exists_hard_function_dag` (book bound `2ⁿ/(10n)`), with the
  p. 115 probabilistic form `BoolCircuit.prob_computableDAG_shannon_le`, proved by the
  book's steps: `BoolCircuit.prob_eval_eq_apply` (`Pr[C(x) = f(x)] = 1/2`),
  `BoolCircuit.prob_computes` / `prob_computes_eq_prod` (`Pr[C computes f] = 2^{-2ⁿ}`, the
  product of the per-input probabilities) and the union bound `BoolCircuit.prob_computableDAG_le_count`
  (`ShannonProbabilistic.lean`).
* p. 108 circuit remarks — Lupanov `O(2ⁿ/n)` (`BoolCircuit.exists_dagCircuit_faninTwo_size_le_div`,
  `Lupanov.lean`); fan-out two (`DAGCircuit.exists_fanoutTwo`, `FanOut.lean`), including
  `¬¬v` buffers under the literal fan-in-exactly-two convention
  (`DAGCircuit.exists_fanoutTwo_notNot`, `5S`; `DAGCircuit.IsStrict.exists_fanoutTwo`,
  `20S`; `StrictFanOut.lean`); the literal Def 6.1 (`DAGCircuit.IsStrict`,
  `Language.inPPoly_iff_inStrictPPoly`); formulas as fan-out-one circuits, both ways
  (`TreeCircuit.toDAG_fanout_le_one`, `DAGCircuit.exists_treeCircuit_of_fanout_le_one`,
  `FormulaFanOut.lean`).
* Def 6.5's literal `⋃_c SIZE(n^c)` — empty (`Language.not_inSIZE_pow`); `P/poly` is the
  literal bound from length 2 on (`Language.inPPoly_iff_eventually`, `PPoly.lean`).

Remaining Chapter-6 items (each documented as a divergence in its file):

* **Thm 6.22, the size hierarchy over the book's `SIZE`** — only the tree-circuit
  analogue exists (`BoolCircuit.treeSize_ssubset`, `Hierarchy.lean`); the DAG version
  needs a DAG-native padding/counting argument on top of `exists_hard_function_dag`.
* **Tree-circuit CKT-SAT** (`Encoding.lean`, `CircuitSat.lean`) carries no `≤ₚ` claim —
  only equisatisfiability and a clause count; the book's Lem 6.11 is the DAG version
  above.
* The `O(T log T)` oblivious simulation (Remark 1.7) is Chapter 1's Phase 5 above; the
  circuits of `P ⊆ P/poly` are quadratic instead, which suffices for every Chapter-6 use.

`cfg.state = none` with no `_iff` lemma. Published hypotheses use it widely (`Build/Catalog`'s
`hlive`, `ClassNP/EXP`, `ClassNP/SAT`, `CookLevin/Hardness`), and consumers read it through its
body, which the convention of 2026-10-26 allows (`policy.md`). **To do:** add `Cfg.halted_iff`
(`Iff.rfl`) with the next API PR that touches `Configuration`; its replay closure is most of the
library, so not alone. New code then cites it where it rewrites.

### FRZ-1: re-run the declaration freezes with qualified names (from gate 78, minor 2; 2026-10-25)

`devtools/seyoon/declfreeze.py` up to v3 keyed declarations by short name. In a file where two
declarations share one (`Contract.trans`, `Segment.trans` and `SafeSegment.trans`, each written
`theorem trans` inside its namespace), only the last of each name was kept on both sides of a
freeze. A statement or body change to an earlier namesake would therefore not have been reported. v4
(2026-10-25) keys by the qualified name. **Done (2026-10-25; `campaign/items/frz1/`): no campaign
freeze missed a change.** A walk over every consecutive pair of versions, on the campaign's
first-parent chain, of all 815 Lean files it changed finds two landings that changed a declaration
v3 could not see. One is PR #2's communication-complexity split (2026-09-30), which is not
campaign work. The other is Diagonal's parameterization (#100), whose freeze used its own
qualified-name script and lists the three new namesakes. The four open PRs gated before v4 change
no colliding name. 13 files collide today, `Build/Contract/Basic` and `Diagonal` among them.

/-
